It is submitted that in the year 2015, plaintiff got the licence from the Department of Food Safety under FSS Act, 2006 for manufacturing and selling of JUICE in the name of "HONEY JUICE and that the label HONEY JUICE is to be used on packing pouch which primary consist of the distinctive features are as under:-
a) The packing pouch primarily a transparent which consists of label "HONEY JUICE"

It is further submitted that defendants are further likely to destroy the plaintiff brand and market in case of quality of the defendants product deficient, inferior and substandard and that on account of illegal, unlawful and nefarious acts on the part of the defendant No. 1 and other persons including other defendants No. 2 to 4 has caused a great deal of loss and injury to the goodwill,
reputation and loss of business opportunities due to the sale marketing of the material.

Plaintiff has also examined PW-3 Sh. Sunil Kumar Chaturvedi who had inspected the premises of defendant no. 1 on 02.06.2018 after taking the police aid and thereafter submitted his report in the court on 06.06.2018.
PW-3 has proved his report alongwith annexures as Ex.PW-3/A and has also proved photographs Ex.PW-3/P-1 to Ex.PW-3/P-29.
He has also proved site plan, Ex.PW-3/P- 30 and seizure memo Ex.PW-3/P-31.It

is urged that on account of loss of business, goodwill reputation, the plaintiff assess his damages to the tune of Rs.15,00,000/- which the defendant is liable to pay for unauthorized and unwarranted use of trade "HONEY JUICE".
37.

Testimony of plaintiff's witnesses has remained unchallenged and evidence on record establishes that defendants are violating the intellectual property rights and infringing trademark/trade name "HONEY JUICE" belonging to petitioner.
In the result, this court finds that plaintiff has discharged the onus and therefore, this issue is decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants.

sentences.text: Onus to prove these issues was upon the defendants.
However, the defendants have failed to appear and discharge their onus.
Hence these issues no. 6 & 7 are accordingly decided in favour of plaintiff and against the defendants.
Whether the plaintiff is entitled to damage to the tune of Rs.15 lakhs?

Counsel for the plaintiff has argued that the plaintiff caused loss of Rs.15 Lac due to the acts of the defendants which cause loss to the reputation and goodwill of the plaintiff in the market as the defendant No. 1 is doing the wrongful business by manufacturing and selling inferior and lower quality in the market since 2016 and on the other hand the plaintiff selling superior quality under the name and style of "HONEY JUICE".
Ld. Counsel has argued that plaintiff caused loss for his reputation and goodwill as such the business is on the bank of close of his business.
It is further submitted that intention of the defendant No. 1 is not good towards the plaintiff.

40. Onus to prove this issue was on the plaintiff. PW-1 has only testified that on account of illegal and unauthorized act of the defendants in passing off the goods with the name of "HONEY JUICE"
and has merely stated that it has caused a great deal of loss and injury to the goodwill, reputation and loss of business opportunities due to the sale/marketing of the material and the same is assessed as Rs.15 lakhs.
Plaintiff or any other witness has not explained or deposed as to how the said loss was assessed Rs.15 lakhs.
PWs have not uttered anything as to how much goods were sold by the defendants or since then the alleged trade mark was being infringed.
There is nothing on record to show the loss caused by the defendant to the plaintiff.

In the present case, since the plaintiff has failed to prove the damages suffered by him and the basis/criteria of assessment,
therefore, it cannot be held that defendants have caused damages to the plaintiff to the tune of Rs.15 lakhs.
This court finds that plaintiff is not entitled to the damages of Rs.15 lakhs or any other amount.
Consequently, this issue is decided against the plaintiff and in favour of the defendants.
41. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to a decree of entitled to seek a decree of permanent injunction against the defendants as prayed for?
OPP In view of the findings on the aforesaid issues, this Court finds that plaintiff is entitled to a decree of permanent injunction , as prayed against the defendants.
42. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to a decree of mandatory injunction?
OPP Plaintiff has not been able to establish about the material in the possession of defendants, who are already exparte.

The plaintiff witnesses have failed to establish about the specific possession of the infringed honey juice ,
labelled blocks by the defendants.
Therefore, no such relief of mandatory injunction for delivering the material, for the purpose of destruction and eraser, as prayed, can be ordered.
RELIEF 43.

In view of aforementioned reasons and findings a decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendants by itself as also through its individuals proprietor, partners, agents, representatives,
distributors, assigns, heirs, successors, stockists and all other acting for and on their behalf from using selling soliciting, exporting displaying, advertising by visual, audio print mode or by any other mode or manner or dealing in or using the impugned "HONEY JUICE" or any other Shri Pawan Kumar vs Shri Israruddin on 31 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113354080/
11 packing/trademark/label identical with and/or deceptively similar thereto in relation to their impugned goods and business and related/allied products and from doing any other acts or deed amounting to or likely to finding and/or violating plaintiff's copyrights in the said trade mark/label "HONEY JUICE"
.

This suit was filed in May, 2018 and trial of the case continued for about two years,
in these circumstances, it is held that plaintiff is entitled to costs comprising of litigation charges & other expenses to the tune of Rs.25,000/-.
Order accordingly.
File be consigned to record room.
